_about: Every failure from the 26 Oct to 1 Nov 2026 runs, the code that now prevents it, and its status. status=enforced means a function, test or workflow step exists and tests/test_failure_ledger.py resolves it. status=open means no code yet; it is listed, not hidden. Add a row whenever a run fails for a reason that could be checked in code.

entries.failure: Cloud gate: brief cover text != selected cover text.
entries.fix: Plan cover text is the single source; preflight compares plan text, selection text and the reviewed sha.

entries.failure: Render checkout lacked anim-point4.mp4 (captures are gitignored; MP4s never tracked).
entries.fix: Every media file a brief names must exist locally (check_assets_present); the capture-packs release copy must exist (check_capture_pack_release).

entries.failure: A capture pack pushed before local files changed would render stale media.
entries.fix: preflight compares local file digests with the bytes last pushed (tracker/capture-pushes.json, written by capture_store push). A workspace restore changes mtimes only and does not block.

entries.failure: Three MP4s tracked in git; storage audit ok:false blocked preflight.
entries.fix: Storage audit blocks over-budget workspaces and tracked videos; the driver never commits MP4s (it commits only briefs, plans, receipts).

entries.failure: Production receipts were typed by hand; a stale brief hash or word count failed the gate.
entries.fix: Receipts are built from the brief and capture manifest and validated before they are written.

entries.failure: origin remote lost after a restore; dispatch check only noted it, so a stale render could start.
entries.fix: Unreadable origin is a BLOCK for cloud dispatch.

entries.failure: git push rejected after the cloud run pushed render-attempt commits to origin main.
entries.fix: The source stage rebases on origin with autostash before pushing, then checks origin == HEAD.

entries.failure: A dispatch piped into head -1 killed the local process after the cloud run was created.
entries.fix: Every subprocess writes to a log file under /var/tmp/reels/make-shorts; nothing is piped into head.

entries.failure: Repeat dispatch within 6 h created a duplicate render and blocked the next one.
entries.fix: reels.py cloud refuses a repeat within 6 h unless --redispatch REASON is given; the driver never passes it.

entries.failure: pytest collected archive/ tests; yt-dlp missing from PATH failed a test.
entries.fix: pytest.ini limits testpaths and skips archive; tests/conftest.py puts ~/.local/bin on PATH.

entries.failure: Hard-coded ffmpeg path in claude_mem_loop.py no longer existed after a package update.
entries.fix: Resolved at run time with imageio_ffmpeg.get_ffmpeg_exe().

entries.failure: Gitignored spec files were silently skipped by git add; preflight tracked gate blocked late.
entries.fix: The source stage uses git add -f on the exact files it needs, then commits only if something is staged.

entries.failure: A schedule run created Buffer posts before the cadence fix (claude-mem), and an earlier run wrote to Buffer without owner go.
entries.fix: The driver dispatches dry-run and verify first; schedule runs only when the request says schedule (or --schedule).

entries.failure: Two videos got the same post time.
entries.fix: Cadence skips any bracket held by a scheduled post on the channel.

entries.failure: Queue approved a video whose brief changed afterwards.
entries.fix: queue pin blocks when the brief hash differs from the approved one.

entries.failure: viewer_panel.py --help treated the flag as an MP4 path.
entries.fix: The driver always passes the MP4 path; the panel verdict must be written by a reviewer (PASS/FAIL file).

entries.failure: YouTube Shorts cover not approved after post was sent.
entries.fix: queue approve requires cover_sha256 for YouTube; the driver waits for cover approval before queueing.

entries.failure: Cloud render failure was only visible after a long wait; the cause was in the log.
entries.fix: The driver tails the log on failure and stops the batch at that stage.

entries.failure: cover_system.py returned rc 2 on a repeat run and rc 0 on identical inputs.
entries.fix: Not yet fixed: the driver checks the return code, but the tool itself is not made deterministic.

entries.failure: dry-run reported No new posts planned because the queue was at capacity, which looked like a bug.
entries.fix: Not yet fixed: the driver prints the planner notes; the capacity message should be made clearer in the tool itself.

entries.failure: SEO warning SP010: the keyword is not spoken in the first ~10 s of the iFixAi script.
entries.fix: Warning only; the owner decides whether it becomes a block. Not changed.

entries.failure: Topics were chosen without an explicit owner approval record.
entries.fix: select only takes topics with an owner approval bound to the plan sha256 (config/topic-approvals.json); the approve command requires the owner's words.

entries.failure: Published briefs kept failing new cloud-source checks they never needed.
entries.fix: config/legacy-briefs.json (from tracker/publications.json, sent or published_manual) turns those checks into notes for legacy briefs.

entries.failure: Radar excluded topics for ToS, piracy or scraping reasons, against the owner's rule.
entries.fix: RISK holds only the sexual/uncensored flag; tests/test_trend_radar_rules.py enforces it.

entries.failure: Platform tiles clipped at the right frame edge (flex min-width blowout on the content pane); pixel-QA passed, owner caught it in the preview.
entries.fix: .mk-pane min-width:0 + fixed sidebar; renderer now audits real layout per scene (clip-ancestor-aware, opacity-gated) and fails BEFORE encoding when an element lands >28px past the frame edge.

entries.failure: VIDEO toggle showed an empty stage with a static play glyph — owner: 'does not show any video; just a play button'.
entries.fix: Video mode is a playing video: animated art, EQ overlay, running timecode, PLAYING badge, one tap-flash. Standing rule: a mode/toggle frame must show the state RUNNING, never a placeholder glyph; the viewer panel bars already fail static stages.

entries.failure: Buffer delivery blocked: 56MB of consumed base64 ext-video staging payloads still tracked in git, tripping the storage budget guard in post.yml.
entries.fix: Staging payloads are released in the same cycle that consumes them (deleted after ext-videos-upload runs succeeded). Budget guard held the line; the miss was lifecycle hygiene, not a missing check.

entries.failure: frame-critique video mode: (a) YouTube/TikTok CDNs refuse runner datacenter IPs (cookies/4xx) so reference videos cannot be downloaded in CI; (b) NVIDIA hosted catalog currently ships NO video-capable model (cosmos-* all 404); (c) dense-1fps fallback works (56 frames logged on video 1) but costs ~25 min/video against flaky free endpoints.
entries.fix: Videos are staged via the ext-videos b64 channel (uploaded from a residential sandbox, decoded in-CI). video_critique auto-detects the empty video catalog and falls back to 1 fps frames + synthesis; use it for deep teardowns only, and rely on local frame inspection (read_file on sampled jpgs) for speed.

entries.failure: Two voice jobs burned full 60-minute timeouts with no signal: the runner's apt mirror DNS (azure.archive.ubuntu.com) failed intermittently and apt retried silently for an hour.
entries.fix: setup-render.sh sections are timed+named (TOOLCHAIN-SECTION markers, kill at budget with TOOLCHAIN-STALL name); setup-sandbox.sh apt calls IPv4-forced with 5x retry and auto-switch sources to archive.ubuntu.com.

entries.failure: SEO pack was evaluated only after a full render, so two complete render cycles (video + QA green) died at the gate.
entries.fix: seo_pack now runs inside brief_from_plan, before a brief is ever written.

entries.failure: The local git dag had a permanently-missing blob (commit 83d5a27 reserves-render-attempt); every push since was sending hollow refs — latent poison for any future fetch/gc. Also workspace was carrying stale render mp4s (~80MB) that Actions artifacts already archived.
entries.fix: tools/housekeeping.py — run before every big op: (1) git fsck must be clean or BLOCK pushes; (2) renders dir keeps only the current 2 builds; (3) 250 MB hard cap. Reset history to one clean snapshot (3abb020) — file state preserved.

entries.failure: Five render cycles shipped text-on-grid shorts: no gate ever looked at the pixels, and the vision critique artifact was never read.
entries.fix: ui_proof_gate measures every referenced asset before render (blank, blank-run, static, no-text, bot wall, optional VLM) and fails the job.

entries.failure: ubuntu-26.04 ships python 3.14 and torch 2.6.0 was purged; pip reported both as missing packages while the toolchain wrapper called every failure a stall.
entries.fix: python pinned to 3.12, torch resolved as >=2.6,<3 from the CPU index, and ran() now separates TIMEOUT from FAILED.

entries.failure: The whole voice stack declares Requires-Python <3.14, so on the runner's default 3.14 pip could only see ancient releases.
entries.fix: ubuntu-26.04 ships python 3.14 and the whole voice stack declares <3.14, so pip could only see ancient releases; .github/workflows/render.yml now pins 3.12 via setup-python in the voice and render jobs, and the toolchain reports TIMEOUT vs FAILED honestly.

entries.failure: ui_proof_gate joined the brief's repo-relative capture path under ROOT, producing captures/captures/<id> and false-failing every asset.
entries.fix: Path resolution accepts absolute, repo-relative and bare-id forms.

entries.failure: A dispatch that died in Toolchain permanently burned the brief's input fingerprint, so every retry was refused as duplicate input.
entries.fix: release subcommand frees reservations from pre-render deaths only, and refuses anything that reached the renderer.

entries.failure: Workspace ballooned to 143MB with stale renders, and the first delivery-cleanup draft would have deleted a live deliverable.
entries.fix: housekeeping prunes stale renders, groups same-window delivery folders as one batch, keeps fsck clean, enforces the 250MB cap.
